## Design for recognition

A logo is not a small illustration of everything an organization does. It is an identifying mark that must remain recognizable across sizes, materials, and contexts. A **lettermark** starts with one or more letterforms and changes their shape, spacing, overlap, or negative space to create a distinctive symbol.

## Development sequence

1. Identify the audience, context, and qualities the mark should communicate.
2. Sketch at least six alternatives before opening vector software.
3. Build two or three candidates using letterforms and simple geometry.
4. Test positive and reversed versions in one colour.
5. Reduce the design until every remaining element has a job.
6. Check it at small size, from a distance, and as an engraved silhouette.

## Negative space

Negative space is the area around and inside shapes. It can separate forms, reveal a second symbol, improve recognition, or create ambiguity. Test by filling the entire logo black. If the important counter-shapes close up, revise the spacing or simplify the form.

## Fabrication constraint

Very thin lines, tiny counters, and detached islands may fail when engraved or cut. Preserve an editable master, then create a fabrication copy in which critical text is converted to paths and small features are checked against the material and machine.

::: {.ter-project-brief}

Create a lettermark and place it with your name inside an exact rectangular plaque. This file becomes the artwork for [Name + Logo: Engrave and Cut](../03-laser-cutting/01-name-logo.qmd).
